subject: general
question:
Replace the underlined word in the given sentence with the most appropriate synonym from the options listed below.

Morality is contextual; therefore, it is foolish to believe that one’s moral judgement would be perfect and __immaculate__ .
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **impeccable**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"immaculate"** means perfectly clean, neat, or tidy; free from flaws or mistakes. (निर्मल)

 
 
• **Example: **Her kitchen was immaculate, with every utensil in its place.
 
 
 
• **"Impeccable"** refers to something that is in accordance with the highest standards of propriety; faultless. (निष्कलंक)
 
 
• **Example: **His manners were impeccable, always polite and respectful to everyone.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the synonym of **'immaculate' **is **'impeccable'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **impeccable**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Grubby **(मैला): Covered with dirt; grimy.

 
 
• **Example:** His hands were grubby after working in the garden all day.
 
 
 
• **Indelicate **(अशिष्ट): Lacking sensitivity or tact; coarse.
 
 
• **Example: **He made an indelicate remark that offended many people at the dinner party.
 
 
 
• **Tarnished** (कलंकित): Having lost its luster, especially as a result of exposure to air or moisture.
 
 
• **Example:** The silverware was tarnished and needed to be polished.
